title: Localized quarantine + priority shepherd for soft-surge events (tenant-level ballast)
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: During a recent soft-surge incident we observed noisy-tenants causing large transient backpressure that led to cascading latency increases across regional pools. This PR introduces a lightweight tenant-level "ballast" (localized quarantine) plus a priority shepherd that gently redirects best-effort traffic into a slowpath pool instead of applying blunt, global SLO relaxations. Goals: 1) contain noisy tenants quickly with minimal collateral impact; 2) preserve strict SLOs for high-priority tenants; 3) enable safe, observable rollouts via a small config surface and feature flag.

What this changes (single-line checklist and summary): - Adds tenant ballast controller that marks tenant sessions as quarantined when local latency and token backlog exceed adaptive thresholds. - Introduces priority shepherd that classifies requests into strict/standard/slowpath and routes them to pre-provisioned fast and slow execution lanes. - Soft-quarantine eviction policy that de-escalates based on moving-window health metrics (no hard tenant disable). - Metrics/tags and new tracing span for tenant-quarantine lifecycles, including reasons and duration. - Admin endpoints to list active quarantines and to manually lift quarantines for debugging.

Implementation notes: The controller runs inside the routing plane (router/service) and subscribes to per-spot latency histograms and in-flight token counters. Thresholds are computed per-tenant using an EWMA of 1m/5m windows with a safety multipler derived from tenant SLA tier. When a tenant crosses the soft-surge boundary, we mark their sessions with quarantine=true and route new requests into the slowpath pool. Existing in-flight requests are allowed to complete to avoid amplification. Quarantine entries are time-boxed and decay through a penalty-decay factor; repeated violations increase decay length (exponential backoff) but never exceed configured hard limit.

Risk and mitigation: The slowpath uses cheaper quantized model variants to reduce cost. To avoid quality regressions we enforce a per-tenant "canary token budget" — a small fraction of requests may still be served via the fast lane for continuous quality checks. The feature is gated behind a runtime flag and rollout is gradual (10% of tenants first, then ramp). Ops runbook added describing emergency rollback (gate=false) and manual quarantine lifting.

Checklist (completed): - [x] Controller logic and adaptive thresholding implemented - [x] Router routing table changes + slowpath pool wiring - [x] Metric and tracing instrumentation - [x] Unit + integration tests for routing decisions - [x] End-to-end staging canary run

Checklist (follow-ups after merge): - [ ] Add dashboard panels for quarantine churn per-region - [ ] Add automated alert for quarantine storm (more than N active quarantines in window) - [ ] Progressive rollout to Dedicated pools (next sprint)

Commits summary: - feat(quarantine): initial ballast controller and config schema - feat(router): attach priority shepherd and slowpath routing - perf: tighten slowpath model selection and batching defaults - test: integration tests for quarantine lifecycle - docs: runbook and config docs

Changed areas (high level): - router/service/router_quarantine.go - controller/tenant_ballast.go - services/slowpath_pool_manager.go - metrics/observability_quarantine.md - tests/integration/quarantine_lifecycle_test.go - ops/runbooks/quarantine-runbook.md - proto/routing.proto (small additions)

CI and validation: All unit and integration suites passed in CI; load tests run in the benchmark-lab staging cluster showed a 62% reduction in cross-tenant latency amplification during injected noisy-tenant scenarios. No regressions in existing latency SLOs for strict-tier tenants.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after address of reviewer comments; feature left behind runtime flag feature.quarantine.tenant_ballast=false by default for safe rollout.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice approach. Please add a unit test for the EWMA threshold computation (edge cases: zero requests and burst reset).

release_notes: Introduces tenant-level soft quarantine and priority routing to limit cross-tenant amplification during soft surges. Administrators can monitor and lift quarantines via an ops endpoint. Rollout is behind a runtime flag. Recommended: enable in staging and monitor quarantine churn dashboards before enabling on production.
notes_for_oncall: If quarantine storms are observed (many tenants quarantined quickly), set feature.quarantine.tenant_ballast=false to disable and investigate with /internal/quarantines output. Use runbook to lift stuck quarantines.
safety_checks: Quality canary: 1% of tenant requests still routed to fast lane for quality verification
Hard caps: per-tenant slowpath rate limit to avoid starving dedicated pools
Observability: new spans and metrics to track reasons and durations
